1  ORDER

The petitioners are the accused Nos.1 and 2 in crime No.688/2020 of Palode Police Station,
Thiruvananthapuram, which is now pending as SC No.476/2021 before the Special Court for SC/ST (POA) Act Cases, Nedumangad.

entities.text: Special Court for SC/ST (POA) Act Cases, Nedumangad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offences alleged against them are under Sections 498A, 376 and 417 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3(1) (S) and 3(2) V(a) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The prosecution case is that the 1 st accused, who is not a member of Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe with the intention to satisfy his sexual lust after promising to marry the defacto complainant who is a member of Scheduled Caste community, committed rape upon her and thereafter he married her and while they were living together as husband and wife he along with the 2 nd accused subjected her to cruelty both physically and mentally and thereby they are alleged to have committed the above offences.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, the matter has been settled amicably and also that the victim is residing 2025:KER:93420 along with the 1 petitioner as husband and wife and no dispute subsists st between them and therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioners.

4. The learned counsel for the defacto complainant also submitted that the matter has been settled and she also prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioners.
5.
The petitioners also produced the marriage certificate issued from the Kalliyoor Grama Panchayat showing that the 1 st petitioner married the defacto complainant on 24.11.2018.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.
7.

The learned Public Prosecutor, upon instructions from the investigating officer submitted that the respondents 3 and 4 had given statements to the investigating officer also upon the same terms as that in the affidavits filed before this Court by respondents 3 and 4.
8.
In the decision in Mahesh Mukund Patel v. State of U.P., 2025 SCC OnLine SC 614, the accused married the victim and they were leading a happy married life.

entities.text: Mahesh Mukund Patel v. State of U.P., 2025 SCC OnLine SC 614
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in that case the victim was a major at the time when the offence was committed.

However, the fact that the person who was once an assailant, now turned out to be the 2025:KER:93420 protector and saviour of the victim was considered as a relevant circumstances to quash the proceeding pending against him.
9. The principles laid down in the above cases can be applied in the facts of the present case also.
In this case also, the 1 st petitioner has already married the victim and now they are leading a happy married life.

Therefore, termination of the proceedings against the 1 st petitioner in such an X vs State Of Kerala on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165038736/
2 exceptional circumstance is highly necessary to maintain the harmonious and peaceful life of the victim who now remains under the care and protection of the petitioner.
Therefore, the prayer for quashing the proceedings against the petitioners deserves favourable consideration.
In the result, this petition is allowed.

The proceedings against the petitioners/accused No.1 and 2 in S.C 476/2021 on the file of the Special Court for SC/ST (POA) Act Cases, Nedumangad, arising from Crime No.688/2020 of Palode Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram stands quashed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
